---
title: "Wind as a Stochastic Process"
description: "From the spectrum of the wind to the power extremum seeking loses, and the design that loses least, under the two IEC turbulence spectra."
---

::: {.research-page}

::: {.research-lead}
The gradient that extremum seeking computes is noisy because the wind is. Its
noise, the scatter it leaves in the gain, and the power that scatter costs all
follow from one number: the wind's spectral density at the dither frequency.
:::

IEC 61400-1 gives two models of that density for the longitudinal wind,
**Kaimal** and **von Karman**. They share the value at zero frequency (for each
model's own integral length scale) and Kolmogorov's $f^{-5/3}$ fall above the
corner, but turn the corner differently, and with the standard's lengths
($340$ m and $147$ m at the NREL 5 MW hub) they disagree by up to $35\%$ at the
dither frequencies that matter. The analysis is therefore worked out twice, on
equal footing. The derivation up to the spectrum (Links A to C) is common to both
decks; from Link D on, every number is computed and checked against simulation
for that deck's spectrum.

::: {.research-paper}

**Presentations**

[Wind as a Stochastic Process: the Kaimal Model →](q5-kaimal.html)

[Wind as a Stochastic Process: the von Karman Model →](q5-vonkarman.html)

:::

| NREL 5 MW, $8$ m/s, $\mathrm{TI} = 10\%$, tracking time one day | Kaimal | von Karman |
|---|---|---|
| IEC length scale $L$ | $340$ m | $147$ m |
| one period's $\sigma(\hat g)$ at $T = 150$ s, predicted | $5.21\times10^{-7}$ | $5.43\times10^{-7}$ |
| best design | $T = 60$ s, $a = 9.1\%$ of $u^\star$ | $T = 60$ s, $a = 9.6\%$ of $u^\star$ |
| power lost by the best design | $0.20\%$ | $0.23\%$ |
| power lost by the published design ($150$ s, $13.6\%$) | $0.38\%$ | $0.40\%$ |

The design rule, and its choice of a $60$ s period, does not depend on which
spectrum is used; the loss it achieves moves by $0.02$ points. Both decks end
with the same comparison section, including the shaping filter with which Lao
et al. (ACC 2022) generate von Karman wind, and why the analysis here
synthesizes from the spectrum directly instead.

:::
